content: Hangouts used to be the best possible alternative to iMessage. It supported conversations on phone, tablet, or computer, with continuity across all devices. The recent updates to Android (specifically the forced and very bad changes to the way that notifications are categorized) has removed a key feature from the app. Now you can no longer use a customized sound per person for your discussion. Only one sound can be selected for the whole app, which means you can't tell who is messaging you by the sound any more. This whole change is very problematic. In Messages, now I can't make group conversations silent. The notifications always show up no matter what I change. Since there is no way to leave a group SMS conversation, I am stuck in chats with people that I can't make silent. That was frustrating enough, but now Hangouts has adopted the same system. I suspect that Google is just slowly making Hangouts worse and worse so that people will stop using it and they can quietly cancel it next year without an complaints. Now, every notification on the phone has the same sound. I can't customize the sounds for individual applications anymore. This is really a step in the wrong direction.

content: Google play services is an awful, awful piece of intrusive and horrible software (I'd even call it malware due to the fact that it cannot be removed, nor can it be "disabled" like many other pieces of google bloatware that come with android). I've gone to great lengths to limit it (removing permissions, disabling access to WiFi and data). However, recently it has been further integrated into the functions of android, meaning that the system and many apps will not function properly if you do not give google play services (and by extension Google Inc. and Alphabet) access to your data. Examples of apps that will cease to function if permissions are restricted are Google Play and Gmail. Due to this, I've had to write my negative review about google play services via my PC. I shall have to seek alternatives to android, maybe open source or windows devices. Lastly, I should note that the text and images in the app description here are misleading. You can not uninstall google play services and the options that according to the image seem to be available (force stop, uninstall) are greyed out. I'd wager you have to either root your device, or remove android entirely to get rid of google play services from your device.

content: Practically speaking it's somewhat limited voice control, which I could do 15+ years ago on my Ericsson phone, albeit the phone had fewer functions back then. It was infinitely more useful when it was Google Now: proactive alerts telling me when I needed to leave for appointments, based on real-time traffic conditions, notifications when there was an issue with my commute. If it's meant to be an assistant let it actively assist me, not be something I have to check manually in the hope that what I need *might* be in some feed somewhere. If I have to go searching for it I may as well just open the relevant app and check there instead. It's also crying out for a name. Something pleasant to say rather than that awkward, guttural K-G-G combo. I'm certain Cortana (RIP) and Alexa were so-named at least in part because it was pleasant to say. Or better still you could let us choose the wake word (and a few more options for its voice, pretty please?) I can't be the only one who wants to call out "Centurion" and hear the dulcet tones of a 70s Cylon reply "by your command". If it actively assisted and was cool and fun to use, it'd be amazing, just now you might as well just call it "phone functions voice control" and give up pretending it's much else.

It's actually a good idea, but the problem is that it severely limits the functionality of the whole work profile apps. For example, it's difficult (or just impossible) to attach a document created in your personal profile into your work Gmail or Google Drive. It's not possible to work on your Google Forms either, since the work profile doesn't create a copy of Chrome or the default browser. You should include the option to integrate apps into the work profile! Thank you!

content: One of the best expressive voices for text-to-speech service. It's speech, expressions, pronunciations, and voices are more close to human than any other speech engine I have tried. I have used it to read and listen to medical textbooks; the pronunciations are impressively accurate. I have purchased Acapela (Laura), Vocalizer Voices, and Cereproc (Megan) TTS engines. Acapela and Vocalizer work offline; however, their pronunciations, speech, expressions, and intonations are not as good as Google. Cereproc (Megan) continued to crash for me during a test run. I have tried a free demo of Amazon Polly; I am not impressed with Amazon Polly. I have also tried the free TTS engine RHVoice; it works offline; however, I did not find it as accurate as Google. The only downside of Google TTS I have noticed is that it does not work offline for reading a Google play eBook.

content: App Grade: C+ If you're looking for an app to get you from one city to another, Google is the way to go! The app does a very good job providing navigation along interstates, highways, and major roads. But if you're looking for navigation to a specific address, what I call micro navigation, the app is lacking. If you need to navigate to an apartment within a large complex, the app does a great job of navigating TO the complex. But when it comes to providing micro navigation: Where do I drive to WITHIN the complex to get closest to the apartment?, the app simply does not provide this functionality. Finding the correct apt can be like trying to find a needle within a haystack. Google Maps also does not take into account private, gated communities. I live near a very large gated community that I deliver items to. When I navigate to a location within that community, the app often wants to direct me to the construction entrance, a locked gate I cannot get through. This particular community requires that all deliveries go through a central guard station. Because I have made several deliveries to this community, I have been granted permission to enter from additional access points. Once I reach the alternate access point, there will be a call box I can press a button on to reach the guard station. After identifying myself and the purpose of my visit, the guard will remotely buzz me in so I can proceed through this entrance. Google Maps needs to accommodate for this. Here's an additional issue: I use Google Maps on a large Android tablet in portrait mode. When I press the green driving direction located at the top of the screen, I can see an additional two (2) driving steps. This is very useful because I want to know upcoming turns so I can better select which lanes to get into. Unfortunately, every time Google Maps needs to recalculate the route, the three (3) lines of directions go away, collapsing back into one (1) line of directions--the next turn I need to make. I'm then forced to re-press the single line of directions to make the additional driving steps reappear. Google, can you add an option so that this does not happen? Since I have a large tablet, I want to have the option to see the next three (3) driving steps at ALL times. Another issue occurs when I perform a search for an address and then Google Maps gives me results for locations halfway across the country. I wish there was a way to tell the app that I want to limit my search results to within a certain radius e.g. 10 miles. This would really help to reduce the number of irrelevant search results. I also wish Google could make the command buttons larger. Once Google has the address to go to, I wish I could press on a large "Directions" button and then press on a large "Start" button to begin the navigation process. When I'm trying to press a small button on a large tablet screen, it can be very frustrating. My finger often misses the button or I press the button and the app doesn't register the press. It would be nice if the app had technology whereby it could sense my approaching finger and make the appropriate button much larger and therefore easier to press. Or if the app just made those two buttons much bigger to begin with. Another frustrating point with the app is that in the BEGINNING when I search for an address, it shows me a beautiful map of the destination. I can often see relevant information such as my destination being the 3rd house on the right after I make a turn onto the final street. Well, once navigation has begun and I get close to the destination, the app happily tells me that I've reached my destination but it doesn't pull up that beginning map that shows the house being the 3rd one on the right. There's also no useful audio such as, "Your destination is the 3rd house on the right. It's a two story brown house with a white picket fence." Other issues: App wants me to make left turns onto heavy traffic streets that are like freeways (traffic light preferred). Some rural areas have terribly wrong directions.

content: My only real use of the Google Street View app, at present, is to submit my spherical panoramas, stiched and edited on my desktop computer, onto Google Maps. This has been done ever since Google disabled Street View submissions from desktop computers, a rather infuriating decision - not everyone uses mobile phones to take panoramas. Anyway, I attempted to take a few panoramas with the app and all have ended in spectacular failiure. It might be a hardware issue with my mobile phone (LG G4), but when taking the panorama, the alignment guides and the already-taken frames drift out of alignment. Eventually you will find that you have covered the full 360 degree rotation on the app, yet in reality you still have another 90 degrees to turn. Practically, this means that every frame is spread apart by a certain distance (albeit corrected in stitching), and a quarter of the panorama is missing! Attempts at covering the tiers above and below will intensify the horror, with one tier rotated 180 degrees from another. The stitching will not repair that, as you can imagine. Needless to say, this behaviour is intolerable and makes panorama-taking entirely impossible. I suspect that either the (very good) image stabilisation system in the camera, or the phone's gyroscopes are meddling with the app's operation. As for viewing panoramas, I noticed that the app had improved slightly since when I last used it for this purpose, with less intrusive "cards". It is still much easier on a desktop computer, however. The investigation into whether all phones are genuinely compatible with this app is required, because the LG G4 evidently is not! My old G3, with less hyperactive stabilisation, worked perfectly. It would also be nice to be able to submit my panoramas to Google Maps from my desktop again, instead of sending them to a comparitively inferior device. It seems logical, but I am probably pushing my luck with that.

Viewing a large playlist takes several minutes to load (used to be instant). Play counts are also gone. I've contacted support twice and it's a frustrating experience that goes through these phases: 1) "everything's there, you just need to learn the new UI" 2) "you must be running and old version of the app or web browser" 3) "ok, we don't have those features, but we want your feedback, so go to help and send a screenshot with details." content: I have a home control network with 40+ devices: lights from different brands, Home speakers, Chromecast devices, etc ... on a 3 puck Google WIFI LAN. I've used Google Home app since inception, and generally been pleased with it. It provides a unified view of devices of same kind from different manufacturers. I had been pleased with the incremental improvements. I would have given 4-5 stars. Not sure which update it was, but at some point Nest devices (like e.g., thermostat) became natively managed by Home app rather than Nest app, and there was an option to move Google WIFI management to Home also rather than WIFI app. No choice on the former, the latter was not reversible (but I did it anyhow). About 2-3 weeks ago it seems, I started seeing strange things. There were various types of anomalies, which I won't list here. The most significant was that the Home Instance, inside the Home App, just disappeared. Along with it, all the Room structure was gone. Some devices which were part of the Home Instance were orphaned within the Home app and some just disappeared. When Home Instance disappears, then so does the means of managing native Home devices, and WIFI (because irreversible) That means rebuilding the LAN from factory reset and re-integrating orphaned and missing devices back into a NEW Home Instance. This is tedious, and I've had to do it 3 times recently. I finished the 3rd yesterday AM and the Home Instance vanished yesterday PM, along with all devices but Home speakers. Then an empty Home appeared. Frustrating, and Home is feeling to me like it needs a good bit more testing. I learned earlier NEVER to delete your Home Instance (strongly advise), since it causes the "dangling devices" problem. I had also earlier decided NOT to migrate WIFI to Home (strongly advise this). Generally, I have backed away from Google Home app (for now) favoring the lower level apps, when possible. I have no idea what is causing this flakiness recently. But I have turned off beta on all Minis and intend to WAIT a good bit of time, until I have some indication that the Google Home app is substantially more stable. I think the Home app may benefit from an architectural review and lots more testing.

content: I am impressed with the scale of compatibility between Google Home and devices on the market. Building a product for the widest possible audience across is impressive. Google crushes Amazon on languages. I wish the the routines allowed for a wider variety of non-verbal triggers. In Europe I cannot use time as a scheduling trigger, this is odd because nearly all of the connected devices/apps have this capability (Bosch, Hue, Brennenstuhl, etc...). I agree with many of the other reviewers when they complain about flakiness in linking new devices. I experiences significant problems adding Bosch Smart Home and others based on, insert random forum, alleged certificate issues. The most successful fix action was to walk away and try again later. I like the shortcuts at the top of the home menu, scrolling through the menu of overly large icons would be maddening without them. I would like greater distinction added for seperate homes. The mixing of routines and devices is frustrating. I really like the way devices can recognize individual users. This has a lot of unrealized potential. I like Google more than Amazon, but Assistant/Home needs to mature.
